 Order

This Bail Application is filed under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.P.C.)
2.
The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.3198 of 2023 of Ernakulam Central Police Station.

The above case is registered against the petitioner alleging offences punishable under Sections 465, 468,
471, 406, 420 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The prosecution case is that the accused is running a real estate business, promised to sold a property to the defacto complainant for a sum of Rs.20,25,000/-.
Thereafter, the accused accepted part payment totaling to Rs.15,42,000/-.

Thereafter, the defacto complainant reached the registration office, the real property owners refused to execute the sale deed stating that the amount collected by the accused was not BA NO. 3113 OF 2024 given to the owners.
Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the offences punishable under the above sections.
The accused was arrested on 19.03.2024.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the case itself is registered based on a private complaint filed by the defacto complainant before the jurisdictional court, which was forwarded under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.

The learned counsel submitted that even if the entire allegations are accepted, there is no criminal offence is made out and the petitioner is ready to abide any condition if this Court grant him bail.
The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
The Public Prosecutor submitted that offence alleged against the petitioner are serious.
6. This Court considered the contention of the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
The petitioner is in custody from 19.03.2024 onwards.
The case is registered BA NO. 3113 OF 2024 based on a private complaint filed by the defacto complainant, which was forwarded to the police under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
After going through the prosecution case and considering the fact that the petitioner is in custody from 19.03.2024, I think this bail application can be allowed on stringent conditions.
7. Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v. Directorate of Enforcement (2019 (16) SCALE 870),
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

sentences.text: 1. Petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
2. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.

The petitioner shall co-operate with the investigation and shall not,
directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
3. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.
4. Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
5. The petitioner shall appear before the investigating officer on all Mondays till final report is filed.
6.

If any of the above conditions are violated by the BA NO. 3113 OF 2024 petitioner,
the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
